question.text: Which of the following entities is NOT eligible to act as a Depository Participant (DP)?

answer.text: A partnership firm engaged in share trading

explanation.text: The Logic: Eligible DPs include banks (including foreign banks), financial institutions, NBFCs, SEBI-registered stock brokers, RTAs, custodians, and clearing corporations. A partnership firm engaged in share trading does not fall under any of these eligible categories prescribed by SEBI. The Trap: Candidates may assume that any entity dealing in securities can become a DP. However, SEBI has prescribed specific categories with minimum net worth requirements. Even within eligible categories, entities must meet prescribed net worth criteria. Cross-Exam Context: DPs also need to implement the maker-checker concept for processing transactions, adding an operational safeguard layer. The net worth requirements differ for brokers, NBFCs, and RTAs. Distributor's Pro-Tip: When selecting a DP for your clients, consider the entity type. Banks often provide seamless integration with banking services, while broker-DPs offer trading convenience. RTAs acting as DPs can be useful for corporate clients dealing with large volumes.
